summary.headline: TANFAC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.3% YoY to INR187 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.3% on sulphur and power cost spikes; HFC-32 commissioning guided for end-Q3 FY27.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 6.3% YoY to about INR187 crore, driven by solar grade DHF ramp-up, though it fell about 3% QoQ. Operating EBITDA was INR28.6 crore (15.3% margin) versus INR29 crore a year ago, hit by elevated sulphur prices and higher power and fuel costs linked to West Asia. PAT fell to INR16.8 crore from INR19.4 crore, also weighed by a deferred tax adjustment. The company completed a INR250 crore QIP, is now net debt-free, and has a proposed ~INR100 crore preferential issue and NSE listing application underway.

segments.name: AHF / HF platform
segments.commentary: HF capacity ~30,000 tpa; Q1 HF plant utilisation 73%, AHF segment ~75%, average AHF realisation INR275-280/kg-equivalent as stated; AHF sold monthly or quarterly with no long-term contracts.

segments.name: Sulphuric acid
segments.commentary: Utilisation ~85-88% in Q1 (about 90% by segment); sulphuric acid prices rose from ~INR20 to INR30-35 with management saying spread to sulphur is unchanged.

segments.name: Solar grade DHF
segments.commentary: Both phases commissioned; running at full capacity, 80-85% volume contracted under long-term contracts through FY29 (about 3.5 years); pricing passes through raw material costs.

segments.name: Specialty fluorides
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 50% across 4-5 products in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at at least 30% YoY, driven by HFC-32 launch in Q4 and existing product utilisation ramp-up.
FY28 revenue growth targeted above 60%, driven by HFC-32 ramp-up and inorganic fluorides.
EBITDA margin guided to 16-19% from the next quarter; about 25% for next year once HFC-32 is operational; management also cited ~30% margin on the new project and ~21-22% blended for FY27.
HFC-32 (20,000 tpa) commissioning guided for end-Q3 FY27 / late November; stabilisation December-January, ramp-up from mid-February.
HFC-32 volume assumed at 65-70% in Q4 FY27 and 80-85% in FY28; management said it is confident of 90%+ utilisation in the coming year.
AHF realisation expected stable for next 4-6 months, subject to sulphur prices.

Broad capex plan of INR1,500-1,700 crore over ~4 years; near-term INR300 crore across solar DHF expansion (INR30-40 crore), AHF (~INR120 crore) and electronic grade (~INR150 crore), with +/-10% tolerance.
capex_capacity: HFC-32 (20,000 tpa): ~60% of work complete; remaining 30-35% to finish by November; machines arriving early September, erection 20-25 days; no cost overrun expected; 22% tax rate applies.
Solar grade DHF: management plans to roughly double capacity; decision pending reactor evaluation; work to start after HFC-32 commissioning, about 6 months lead time.
AHF: planned addition of 20,000-30,000 tpa, commissioning expected in FY28 (about 12-15 months lead time).
Electronic grade (semicon) capex ~INR150 crore; technology tie-ups under evaluation, with one MoU-level partner being assessed.
R&D capex INR7-8 crore over last 1.5 years; revenue-nature R&D spend INR5-6 crore.
demand_pricing: Q1 revenue growth split: ~15% pricing and ~6-8% volume, per management.

HFC-32 contracts cover ~65% of 20,000 tpa capacity, 5-7 year terms, ~75% exports; Japanese customer is a firm contract, domestic OEM described as near-contract, and a 5,000 t MoU expected to convert; all take-or-pay per management.
HFC-32 contract price ~$5.5/kg, formula-linked to input costs; management expects prices to soften to $6-7 range in 1-1.5 years versus peer spot prices cited by an analyst at $9-10.
Indian AHF domestic demand estimated at 30,000-35,000 tpa; Chinese AHF imports seen as limited due to export licensing and ISO tank logistics.
Sulphur price moved from ~INR30 to ~INR105 per management; price pass-through lag 30-45 days. Fluorspar sourced from South Africa, Vietnam, Thailand.

qa_highlights.question: Sulphur sourcing and margin range for FY27 with HFC-32 in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sulphur availability is not an issue and cost increases pass through with a 30-45 day lag; EBITDA margin guided 16-19% from next quarter, ~25% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth price-led or volume-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 15% pricing and 6-8% volume growth, averaging about 6% overall as stated.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans beyond HFC-32?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term ~INR300 crore: solar DHF INR30-40 crore, AHF ~INR120 crore, electronic grade ~INR150 crore; long-term plan to be decided in 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the HFC-32 contract price ~$5.5 versus peers' spot prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritised speed to market, placed 65% of volume early on formula-based pricing, and expects prices to soften to $6-7; remaining ~30% to be sold spot.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power and fuel costs and employee costs move QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Power costs rose on a one-off basis due to West Asia pricing and captive power plant being down for sulphuric acid maintenance; employee cost fell versus last year's one-off bonuses; expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D/electronic grade strategy and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Evaluating technologies with tie-ups; semicon approval cycle 1-1.5 years; HFOs and high-performance fluoropolymers after 2.5-3 years, with project announcements in FY28 for execution by 2029-30.

risks_watch: HFC-32 commissioning timeline: remaining 30-35% of construction due by November, machines arriving early September, erection 20-25 days; any slip pushes the Q4 FY27 volume ramp (65-70% assumed) and the FY27 growth guidance of at least 30%.

Sulphur price pass-through: sulphur moved from about INR30 to INR105 with a 30-45 day lag; sulphuric acid to AHF spread also carries a 30-40 day lag. Watch whether the 16-19% margin guidance from next quarter is met.

Contract quality for HFC-32: 65% contracted with the Japanese customer as firm, domestic OEM described as near-contract, and a 5,000 t MoU yet to convert; 30% is left for spot pricing against an expected softening to $6-7/kg.
Power and fuel cost normalisation in Q2 FY27 after captive power plant downtime and West Asia-linked pricing; deferred tax impact on PAT and effective tax rate normalisation.
Solar grade DHF expansion (planned near doubling) depends on a pending reactor evaluation; electronic grade technology tie-up still under evaluation, with a 1-1.5 year semicon approval cycle.
Ramp-up risk: management plans a vertical startup with stabilisation December-January and ramp from mid-February; no teething losses were explicitly built into guidance.
key_quotes: Current sulphur price increased from about INR30 to INR105 as of now, but the availability of sulphur is not an issue.
So, my 65% is sold at a fixed EBITDA margin which I'm certain of. There's no volatility there.
I'm confident of getting 90% plus utilization in the coming year.
So, we are evaluating the various technologies which are available there and then we'll take a call how to -- which one to take and how to go and all.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth, HFC-32 timelines and contract visibility, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term margins, with sulphur and power costs described as temporary. It declined to comment on competitors in solar grade and kept electronic grade technology partners and fluoropolymer products confidential.
